title: Equal Row and Column Pairs
summary: For a given n x n integer matrix grid, count the number of pairs consisting of a row index and a column index where the corresponding row and column have identical elements in the same order.
statement: For a given n x n integer matrix grid, count the number of pairs consisting of a row index and a column index where the corresponding row and column have identical elements in the same order.
constraints: A row-column pair is equal only when all values match in the same order.
Count index pairs, so duplicate equal rows or columns contribute separately.
hints: Represent each row as an immutable tuple.
Count duplicate row tuples in a frequency map.
Transpose with zip to obtain each column tuple, adding its row frequency.
For every column, the frequency is exactly the number of row indexes forming an equal pair with it.
editorial: For every column, the frequency is exactly the number of row indexes forming an equal pair with it.

tests.explanation: Only the first row equals the first column.
Duplicate matching rows and columns produce three index pairs.
